display.purpose: Page titles and the hero name. Archivo Black, fluid clamp, tight tracking, 0.88-0.95 line-height — structural, not decorative.

headline.purpose: Section and project titles. Archivo Black at the smaller clamp.

body.purpose: Running text, bios, case-study copy. Archivo 300-400 at 15px.

body-sm.purpose: Descriptions, chat messages, dense metadata. Archivo 400 at 13px.

label.purpose: JetBrains Mono 500, 11px, 0.18em. Nav, footer, tags, years, indices, captions — the whole information layer.

label-wide.purpose: JetBrains Mono 500, 11px, 0.28-0.35em. Eyebrows and section markers.

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: Universal easing for all entrances and transitions. Arrives fast, lands clean. Used at 0.5–0.9s for reveals, 0.2–0.3s for state changes.

motion.name: stagger-children
motion.purpose: Staggered entrance for list items (mobile nav links). Applied as Framer Motion stagger.

motion.name: spring-image
motion.purpose: Spring animation for Lightbox image transitions only. Not used elsewhere.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Mobile nav collapses to full-screen overlay below this.

breakpoints.name: shell-max
breakpoints.purpose: section-shell max-width. Content centers and adds 1rem gutter each side below this.

a11y.contrastFloor: 4.5:1 for every text colour, verified against #000000 and #0D0D0D
a11y.typeFloor: 11px — no text below it, screen or print
notes: text-dim (2.28:1) is a structural mark colour and must never carry text.
grey-500 was raised from #6B6560 (3.66:1) to #827C75 (5.09:1) on 29 Aug 2026; it is the site-wide secondary label colour, so the token moved rather than the call sites.
Hero labels sit on two gradient legibility bands, not on the flat scrim alone.
prefers-reduced-motion removes travel and looping but keeps 120ms colour/opacity feedback.
Anything that opens the lightbox is a real <button>.

components.name: Primary CTA Button

narrative.overview:
This portfolio does not perform. It works. The visual system is built the way a production is built: structure first, then everything else earns its place. The dark shell (OKLCH hue 250, near-zero chroma) is not dramatic — it is neutral in the same way a black stage is neutral. It holds the work without comment.

The Warm Signal accent (hue 35, amber) appears where action is required. Buttons. Hover states on navigation. Text selection. It is never decorative. Its rarity is its authority.

Motion is controlled and calibrated. The custom ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) governs every entrance. Elements arrive with confidence and stop cleanly. Nothing bounces. Nothing elastic.
keyCharacteristics: Single-hue dark shell (hue 250) with one warm accent (hue 35), maximum contrast distance
Single type family (Archivo + Archivo Black), hierarchy through weight and scale only
Flat elevation — depth via tonal surface steps, no shadows
Motion is sparse, purposeful, and exponential-ease only
Spacing varies by context; monotony is prohibited

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The Warm Signal accent appears on ≤10% of any given screen surface. If it feels like it's competing for attention, it has been overused. Reduce.

rules.name: The Tint Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries OKLCH hue 250 at chroma 0.01–0.014. Nothing in this system is pure grey. The tint is subtle enough to be invisible in isolation and visible the moment something untinted appears beside it.

rules.name: The Single-Family Rule
rules.body: No additional typefaces. Solve hierarchy through weight contrast and scale, not a second family.

rules.name: The Scale Rule
rules.body: At least a 1.25 ratio between adjacent hierarchy steps. Flat scales read as indecision.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If a component needs to feel elevated, reach for the next tonal surface step — not a shadow.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: The one backdrop-blur on the nav header is functional and at its limit. Do not extend glassmorphism to any other component.

dos: Do use the Warm Signal accent on ≤10% of any screen surface. Its rarity is its authority.
Do vary spacing by context. Section padding, component padding, and inline spacing should all be different.
Do use tonal surface steps (bg → surface → surface-elevated) to express depth. Never shadows.
Do use exponential ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for all motion. Never bounce, never elastic.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion. FadeIn already implements this — keep it.
Do keep nav links, labels, and captions uppercase with wide tracking (0.15–0.30em).
Do tint every neutral toward hue 250.
Do cap body line length at 65–75ch on reading contexts.
donts: Don't use colorful or expressive-color palettes — no gradients, no vibrant accents beyond the single Warm Signal, no neon.
Don't build a generic photographer portfolio layout: no centered hero with soft sans, no pastel tones.
Don't over-animate. If the animation is about the UI, it has failed.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe on any component.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Prohibited.
Don't apply glassmorphism decoratively. The nav header is at the limit.
Don't add shadows. If something needs elevation, use the next surface step.
Don't make the accent compete. If more than 10% of a screen surface carries the Warm Signal, scale it back.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing. Exponential ease-out only.
